name: gtx1060
description: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (GP106, Pascal, sm_61) at its 1506 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SM; the SM is GP104's (gtx1080).

sources.SM (all core knobs): Inherited from gtx1080: GP106 uses the same Pascal SM as GP104 (128 CUDA cores, 32 LD/ST, 32 SFU, 4 FP64, 96 KB shared memory, 48 KB L1/texture)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_BANKS: 1.5 MB L2 in 12 slices (6 x 32-bit controllers, 2 slices each): 24 ways over power-of-two sets, 8 banks
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 192-bit GDDR5 at 8 Gbps (192 GB/s) modelled as 8 GDDR6 x16 channels at 12000 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 8 x 2 B x 12 GT/s = 192 GB/s, the card's bandwidth; latency not calibrated
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1506 MHz base clock (1708 MHz boost), base as in gtx1080
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies as in gtx1080 (Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1, Tesla P4: the same Pascal SM, L1 and L2 design)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 26 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 82-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 52 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the 216-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Not set: no DRAM latency is published for this part, so dram_cycles is unchecked
